application_guidance.input_pattern: An exact zero of the deterministic field under differentiability and inner strong convexity.

Replacing exact zeros by approximate or stochastic zeros; a quantitative error argument is then required.
sensitive_conditions: All three exact directions must vanish.
The Hessian must be invertible and the implicit derivative justified.
A stationary point of h need not minimize h.

content.intended_use: Convert an exact joint-field zero into bilevel stationarity.

proofs.full_local_argument: Fix x. Strong convexity gives G(z,x)>=G(0,x)+<grad_1 G(0,x),z>+(mu_x/2)||z||^2. The right side tends to infinity as ||z|| tends to infinity. Continuity therefore gives an attained minimizer, and strong convexity makes it unique. The first-order condition is grad_1 G(z*(x),x)=0. Conversely, if Dz(z,v,x)=0, strong convexity gives G(u,x)>=G(z,x)+(mu_x/2)||u-z||^2 for every u, so z=z*(x). At this z the symmetric matrix H=H(z*(x),x) satisfies H>=mu_x I and is invertible. Dv=0 now gives v=-H^(-1)grad_1 F(z*(x),x)=v*(x). To justify the hypergradient identity explicitly, apply the implicit function theorem to q(z,x)=grad_1 G(z,x). Since q is C1 and its z derivative H is invertible, near every x there is a C1 solution of q=0. Uniqueness of the minimizer identifies these local solutions with z*, so z* is C1. Writing B=grad^2_21 G at (z*(x),x), differentiation of q(z*(x),x)=0 gives J_z*=-H^(-1)B^T. The chain rule and symmetry of H yield grad h=grad_2 F+J_z*^T grad_1 F=grad_2 F-B H^(-1)grad_1 F=grad_2 F+B v*. At the identified states this is exactly Dx(z,v,x). Since Dx=0, grad h(x)=0. This proves the stated implication for every triple.

map: Strong convexity gives existence and uniqueness of z*(x), and Dz=0 identifies it.
The positive definite inner Hessian and Dv=0 identify v*(x).
Implicit differentiation and the chain rule identify Dx at the exact states with grad h.
proofs.omitted_details: None in this reconstructed argument. It uses elementary strong-convexity facts, the implicit function theorem and the chain rule with their relevant hypotheses stated above.
proofs.reading_coverage: Actually read and visually checked Proposition 2.1, Eqs. (1)–(6), and derivative orientation on original-page images 1–3. No claim of reading a source proof in supplementary material.

assumptions: F is continuously differentiable and G is twice continuously differentiable on R^p x R^d. These are explicit sufficient regularity hypotheses for the source's implicit-differentiation identities; the paper's later Assumptions 3.1–3.2 are stronger.
For every x in R^d, G(.,x) is strongly convex: there exists mu_x>0 such that its Hessian is at least mu_x I at every z. A common uniform constant over x is not required for this identity.
statement.conclusion: Dz(z,v,x)=Dv(z,v,x)=Dx(z,v,x)=0 implies z=z*(x), v=v*(x), and grad h(x)=0.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let F,G:R^p x R^d -> R. Set z*(x)=argmin_z G(z,x), h(x)=F(z*(x),x), H(z,x)=grad^2_11 G(z,x) in R^(p x p), B(z,x)=grad^2_21 G(z,x) in R^(d x p). Define v*(x)=-H(z*(x),x)^(-1)grad_1 F(z*(x),x). At any (z,v,x), Dz=grad_1 G(z,x), Dv=H(z,x)v+grad_1 F(z,x), Dx=B(z,x)v+grad_2 F(z,x).
statement.parameter_domains: p,d positive integers; mu_x positive for each x. No accuracy, iteration, batch-size or probability parameters.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such F,G and every (z,v,x) in R^p x R^p x R^d, if all three exact directions vanish, the conclusion holds. This is deterministic and concerns exact directions, not one random realization of their estimators.

summary: A zero of the exact three-state vector field identifies the exact inner minimizer and auxiliary linear-system solution, and hence a stationary outer point; not a convergence or complexity theorem.
title: Zeroes of the SOBA/SABA vector field imply bilevel stationarity
use_when: Identify what an exact joint vector-field zero means under explicit inner convexity and regularity hypotheses.
